extracted.intended_audience: federal agency officials, administrative lawyers, policymakers, and agency rulewriters
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for how federal agencies must define themselves, publish information, conduct rulemaking and adjudications, provide public access to records/decisions, and afford procedural protections to parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of the Act / overall aims
rubrics_metrics.description: Designed to provide for publicity of information, fairness in administrative operation, and adequacy of judicial review; to assure administration through published procedures which protect private interests, make only reasonable authorized regulations, settle disputes according to law and evidence, confer benefits impartially, and effectuate Congress' policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains the bill's intent: public procedures, protection of private interests, reasonable regulations, settlement by law and evidence, impartial conferring of benefits, and full effectuation of congressional policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Agency' (Section 2(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The word 'agency' is defined by excluding legislative, judicial, and territorial authorities and by including any other 'authority' whether or not within or subject to review by another agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies are defined by the authority to act rather than mere form (departments, boards, etc.); delegations of authority provided by law are not repealed; expressly exempted are (1) agencies composed of representatives of parties or organizations of parties and (2) defined war authorities or civilian authorities functioning under temporary or named statutes. Agencies cannot avoid requirements (e.g., examiner system) simply by form. Exemptions are limited and do not affect public-information requirements of section 3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Person' and 'Party' (Section 2(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Person' includes specified forms of organizations other than agencies. 'Party' includes anyone named, admitted, or seeking and entitled to be admitted as a party in any agency proceeding, but agencies may admit persons as parties for limited purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition ensures individuals and public/private organizations (not federal agencies) are persons; agencies may admit parties for limited purposes but cannot ignore or prejudice the rights of true or full parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Rule' and 'Rule Making' (Section 2(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Rule' is any agency statement of general or particular applicability and future effect designed to implement, interpret, or prescribe law, policy, organization, procedure, or practice requirements; includes prescriptions for future rates, wages, financial structures, etc. 'Rule making' means agency process for formulation, amendment, or repeal of a rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes rules (future conduct prescriptions) from orders (past/existing rights); definition determines whether section 4 (rulemaking) or section 5 (adjudication) applies; enumerates activities to avoid doubt; rulemaking is exempted from some hearing/decision requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Order' and 'Adjudication' (Section 2(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Order' means the final disposition of any matter other than rule making, including licensing, whether affirmative, negative, injunctive, or declaratory. 'Adjudication' means agency process for formulation of an order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Order' intentionally excludes rules; licensing is included because it pronounces present rights of named parties; adjudication covers determinations of present rights or liabilities, including injunctive remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'License' and 'Licensing' (Section 2(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: 'License' includes any form of required official permission such as certificate, charter, etc. 'Licensing' includes agency process respecting grant, renewal, modification, denial, revocation, etc., of a license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes initial licensing from renewals or other licensing proceedings; included because licensing takes many forms and is relevant to other provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Sanction' and 'Relief' (Section 2(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Sanction' includes any agency prohibition, withholding of relief, penalty, seizure, assessment, requirement, restriction, etc. 'Relief' includes any agency grant, recognition, or other beneficial action taken on application or petition of any person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions identify the diverse forms of agency authority relevant to section 9 (sanctions) and section 10 (judicial review); they define but do not confer powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Agency Proceeding' and 'Agency Action' (Section 2(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Agency proceeding' means any agency process defined in subsections (c), (d), or (e). 'Agency action' includes an agency rule, order, license, sanction, relief, the equivalent or denial thereof, and failure to act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terms simplify later language, assure coverage of all forms of administrative procedure or authority, and include supporting procedures, findings, conclusions, or statements of reasons or basis for action or inaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public information required; limited exceptions (Section 3 intro)
rubrics_metrics.description: All administrative operations should as a matter of policy be disclosed to the public except as secrecy may obviously be required or only internal agency 'housekeeping' arrangements may be involved; section 3 requires disclosure except for matters requiring secrecy in the public interest or relating solely to internal management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The public is entitled to know agency procedures and methods; exceptions are narrow and must be clearly and directly involved; neither exception supersedes other legal requirements of publicity or accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules to be published (Section 3(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Every agency must publish in the Federal Register its (1) organization and delegations of final authority and places/ways of doing business with the public, (2) methods of rule making and adjudication including rules of practice, and (3) substantive rules, policies, or interpretations framed for guidance of the public (but not rules addressed to named parties). No person may be required to resort to organization or procedure not so published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication must be kept up to date; separate classes of informational rules (procedure vs substance) should be stated separately; only final delegations of authority must be published under (1), other delegations shown in (2); agencies must state stages/steps and alternatives for types of functions; forbids secrecy of rules binding on the public; forms may be summarized with availability stated; rules should not unnecessarily repeat statutes but identify statutory authority invoked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opinions, orders, and rules to be available to public inspection (Section 3(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies are required to publish or, pursuant to rule, make available to public inspection all final opinions or orders in adjudication of cases (except those held confidential for good cause and not cited as precedents) and all rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should publish or state how to consult decisions/orders/rules; agency must formulate and publish rules respecting access; 'rulings' if authoritative would be covered by section 3(a); exceptions for confidential opinions do not repeal other legal publication requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility of public records (Section 3(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as statutes provide otherwise or information is confidential for good cause, matters of official record are to be made available to persons properly and directly concerned in accordance with agency rules to be issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must classify data, specify what may be disclosed and what may not, provide where applications for information may be made, how they will be determined, and what public agents will do so; refusals subject to section 6(d). The requirement aims to make public records uniformly available and determinable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope/exceptions to rule making requirements (Section 4 intro)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 4's requirements do not apply to rule making involving (1) military, naval, or foreign-affairs functions or (2) matters relating to agency management or personnel or to public property, loans, grants, benefits, or contracts, to the extent those subjects are clearly and directly involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions do not relieve agencies from other statutory requirements; 'foreign affairs' is narrowly construed (those affecting relations with other governments); exceptions permit discretion to dispense with mandatory procedures where proprietary/management matters make them impracticable, but do not preclude voluntary public procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of rule making (Section 4(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: General notice of proposed rule making must be published in the Federal Register — unless all persons subject to the rules are named and personally served or otherwise have actual notice — and must include (1) the time, place, and nature of proceedings, (2) reference to the authority under which held, and (3) the terms, substance, or issues involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice must fairly apprise interested persons of issues so they may present relevant data or argument; legal authority must be specified with particularity (general statutory language is insufficient); agencies may find good cause to dispense with notice for interpretative rules, policy statements, organizational rules, emergencies, or where notice is impracticable/unnecessary/contrary to public interest — but such findings must be made and published and are not an escape clause; agencies should conduct nonpublic studies prior to public procedures to formulate issues and may issue summaries/reports to aid public comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public procedures in rule making (Section 4(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: After notice, the agency must afford interested persons an opportunity to participate in the rule making at least by submitting written data, views, or argument; after consideration of such submissions the agency must incorporate in any rules adopted a concise general statement of their basis and purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This states the minimum requirements short of statutory hearings; agencies may also use advisory committees, informal hearings, conferences, or other procedures; agencies must keep a record, analyze and consider all relevant matters presented, and ensure the statement of basis and purpose reasonably fully explains actual basis and objectives of the rule; applicability of these procedures must be incorporated in rules published pursuant to section 3(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Future effective date of rules (Section 4(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication or service of any substantive rule must be made not less than 30 days prior to its effective date except (1) where the agency finds and publishes good cause or (2) in the case of rules recognizing exemption or relieving restriction, interpretative rules, and statements of policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 30-day deferred effective date is a minimum but not a maximum; agencies may set longer periods where advisable. Good cause exception requires legitimate grounds supported in law and fact and must be published. Some rules (e.g., certain agricultural orders) may be effective sooner due to urgency or unavoidable time limits; no rule requiring action may be made effective until a legally reasonable time after issuance judged in light of circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions respecting rules (Section 4(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Every agency is required to accord any interested person the right to petition for the issuance, amendment, or repeal of a rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agency must fully and promptly consider petitions and take such action as required, and pursuant to section 6(d) notify the petitioner if the request is denied. Filing a petition does not require the agency to grant it, hold a hearing, or engage in public procedures; the agency may grant the petition, initiate public rulemaking per sections 4(a) and 4(b), or deny it. Agency action on petitions must follow procedures published under section 3(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of Section 5 — when adjudication provisions apply
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 5's adjudication provisions apply only where a case is required by statute to be determined upon an agency hearing, except that certain classes of operations are expressly not affected: (1) cases subject to trial de novo in court, (2) selection or tenure of public officers other than examiners, (3) decisions resting on inspections, tests, or elections, (4) military/naval/foreign-affairs functions, (5) cases in which an agency is acting for a court, and (6) certification of employee representatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The section is limited and exceptions apply only 'to the extent' the excepted subject is clearly and directly involved; explanations justify each exception (e.g., trial de novo makes agency determinations only prima facie, personnel selection is discretionary, inspections/tests don't lend themselves to hearings, foreign affairs rare/unsuited to hearings, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notices for adjudications (Section 5(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons entitled to notice of an agency hearing must be informed timely of (1) the time, place, and nature of the hearing, (2) the legal authority and jurisdiction under which it is held, and (3) the matters of fact and law asserted. Where private persons are the moving parties, respondents must give prompt notice of issues controverted in law or fact; agencies may require responsive pleading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issues must be specified with reasonable particularity so parties can prepare; statement of issues in general statutory language is insufficient; agencies must consider convenience and necessity of parties when fixing times/places.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjudication procedure and opportunity for settlement (Section 5(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies are required first to afford parties an opportunity for the settlement or adjustment of issues (where time, nature of proceeding, and public interest permit) and, to the extent issues are not settled, to resolve them by hearing and decision under sections 7 and 8.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary settlement-by-consent may cover whole or part of a case; agencies must state settlement procedures in their rules per section 3(a). Limitations (time, nature, public interest) prevent requiring settlement where impracticable (e.g., many parties or immediate execution required). Where settlements don't dispose of whole case, full hearing/decision procedures apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of prosecuting and deciding functions (Section 5(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Officers who preside at the taking of evidence must make the decision or recommended decision and may not consult with any person or party except openly upon notice (save customary ex parte matters); they may not be subject to supervision by prosecuting officers. Prosecuting officers may not participate in decisions except as witness or counsel in public proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose is to prevent investigating/prosecuting officers from influencing hearing/deciding officers; separation must be reflected in organizational/procedural rules under section 3(a). Exemptions include initial license applications, validity/application of utility rates/facilities/practices, and top agency members; exemptions are narrow and should not be interpreted to permit unfair procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaratory adjudications (Section 6(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Every agency is authorized in its sound discretion to issue declaratory orders with the same effect as other orders, but only where the agency is empowered by statute to hold hearings and the subject is not otherwise exempted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies are not required to issue declaratory orders merely because requested; sound discretion precludes improvident orders; declaratory orders are governed by same principles as declaratory judgments in courts, do not bind non-parties or determine unpresented subject matter, and are subject to judicial review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ancillary matters do not override other provisions (Section 6 intro)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions of section 6 relating to incidental or miscellaneous rights, powers, and procedures do not override contrary provisions in other parts of the bill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This limitation is to prevent, for example, the right of appearance from authorizing improper ex parte conferences during formal hearings under sections 7 and 8; section 6 contains procedural rights incidental to rulemaking or adjudication or independent of either.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appearance or representation of parties (Section 6(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person compelled to appear in person before any agency or its representative is entitled to counsel. In other cases, every party may appear in person or by counsel. So far as orderly conduct of public business permits, any interested person may appear before any agency or its responsible officers at any time for presentation or adjustment of any matter. Agencies are to proceed with reasonable dispatch with due regard for convenience and necessity of parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a statutory and mandatory right; nonlawyers representing parties are neither recognized nor denied by this subsection; agencies must allow appearance in formal, informal, public, or private matters and conclude matters with reasonable dispatch.
